title: Relationships between cytokines and cognitive function from pre- to post-chemotherapy in patients with breast cancer
notes: Longitudinal pilot study from pre- to post-chemotherapy. IL-6, MCP-1, sTNFRI, sTNFRII increased during chemo. IL-6 change associated with worse executive function (OTS) and verbal fluency (Category Fluency). MCP-1 change associated with worse exec function. Best edge: ER_OIC_WORKMEM from OTS-executive-planning proxy. Category Fluency → verbal fluency not extracted (ER_OIC_VERBAL_FLUENCY not in registry). Verbal memory (VRM) results not significant (p=0.105). Baseline IL-6 associated with BETTER post-chemo cognition (paradoxical, possibly adaptive priming). Covariates: age, race, education, baseline reading score, baseline anxiety.
unmapped_findings: ΔIL-6 → ΔCategory Fluency: β=−0.548, SE=0.255, p=0.036 — no ER_OIC_VERBAL_FLUENCY edge in registry
ΔMCP-1 → ΔOTS: β=0.017, SE=0.006, p=0.006 — MCP-1 not a separate node; absorbed into OIC composite
Baseline IL-6 → better post-chemo exec function (paradoxical direction, not extracted)
